figures.caption: Figure 4: Merlin abdominal CCP circuits by finding category (Figure 2c grouping). Each row is one of Merlin’s 11 clinical categories (30 findings total). Columns show embed coordinates with highest category-level selectivity (max AUROC−0.5 across findings in that category; valid split). Color intensity = selectivity.
Figure 2: Sparsity recovery: test classification AUROC vs. number of top channels per finding. A handful of channels recover most of the full-feature performance on Pillar-0.

Figure 3: Causal ablation on CT-RATE validation with frozen Pillar-0. Row c: AUROC changes after zeroing source finding c’s dev-ranked top-K=10 circuit (Sabl c = SK c ); column c′: scored finding. Cell (c, c′) shows ∆c→c′ from Eq. 5. A strong diagonal indicates selective necessity; off-diagonal blocks indicate shared circuits among related findings.

Table 1: Multi-abnormality classification (classification metrics: mean AUROC; mean per-finding weighted F1, accuracy, and precision (PR) after ROC upper-left thresholds on calibration set: CT-RATE official test set (n=1564) and RadChestCT (n=3630). §CT-CLIP rows extracted from Hamamci et al. (2026); †Pillar ClassFine: trained on CT-RATE train labels (∼39k volumes); encoder frozen. ∗zero-shot: Hamamci et al. (2026) present/absent prompt pairs ("c is present." / "c is not present.") embedded with each backbone’s text encoder, scored against cached xi via softmax over two cosines —the same recipe as cited CT-CLIP zero-shot, applied to Pillar-0 (1152-d) or Merlin (512-d, Clinical-Longformer); no label training. ‡CCP-10: training-free channel probe + calibration set thresholds. Bold = best supervised per column; bold underline = best training-free per column.
